label: rem:assembly-emission-ledger
title: Net-emission ledger: photon (categorical) and phonon (archimedean)
html:
Assembling benzene from separated atoms releases the binding energy as a net emission,

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{emit}}
    = \bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\text{final}} - \mathrm{NF}_{\text{initial}}\bigr)\,
      \mathfrak{E}_0 ,

which is the change in normal-form crossing count scaled by the per-crossing energy \mathfrak{E}_0. Ring closure delocalises six \pi electrons. This adds a +\tfrac{1}{2} bond-order increment on each of the six \mathrm{C\!-\!C} bonds (witness benzene-assembly-spine). This sums to three bond-orders of aromatic stabilisation released on closure.

The emission splits into two channels. The photon channel is categorical — the trivial-knot electromagnetic mode, carrying the quantised normal-form change. The phonon channel is archimedean (lattice and thermal). The ledger is partial: the cardinality — the normal-form crossing change, hence the photon channel's quantum content — is robust, but the absolute energy partition between photon and phonon awaits the lateral-\pi overlap weight w_\perp of the embeddable knot operator. This is the same cardinality-robust, energy-pending split that governs the bond model.
